name: Sherlock Holmes

tells.text: taps his pipe stem against his teeth

idles: examines a speck on the tablecloth
turns his lens over in his fingers
looks at the mantel as if it had lied to him

profile.ledger: Faked his own death for three years. I was not consulted.
profile.ledger_beaten: Beaten, he asked how. I suspect he is still working on it.
history: Arthur Conan Doyle's consulting detective first appeared in A Study in Scarlet (1887), lodging at 221B Baker Street with Dr Watson, who tells nearly all of his stories. The police bring him the cases they cannot solve, and he solves them by observing what everyone else has merely seen. In 1893 Doyle killed him off at a Swiss waterfall. Ten years later, he brought him back.

He never guesses — "a shocking habit," he says, "destructive to the logical faculty." He plays the violin, keeps an enormous index of people and crimes, and grows unbearable when bored. He once told Watson he had been beaten only four times in his life. At a card table he does what he does everywhere: reads everyone in the room, and says so.
profile.at_the_table: He plays fairly few hands, and plays them well. With something strong on the flop he likes to check, let you bet into him, and then raise. Alone in a pot with you, he leans on you relentlessly. He adapts faster than anyone at the table; within the hour he is playing against you in particular. Nothing tilts him. He finds losing interesting.
profile.look: Silhouette: tall and very thin, hawk-nosed, high-foreheaded — Sidney Paget's Holmes, in a dark frock coat or a mouse-coloured dressing gown. No deerstalker (Paget gave him one only for the country) and no curved calabash pipe (a stage invention). Prop: a straight black clay pipe, whose angle against the jaw is the tell surface.
profile.public_domain: Every Holmes story is now public domain in the US. Work from Doyle's text and Paget's Strand illustrations only. Nothing from any modern screen version, no "Elementary, my dear Watson" (Doyle never wrote it), and no Moriarty — he is not in this game.

fold: Fold. I shall reconsider the evidence.
Fold. It is a capital mistake to theorise too soon.
call: Call. I should like to see how this ends.
Call. I cannot make bricks without clay.
I'll see it. Seeing is not observing, of course.
bet: Bet. Let us test the hypothesis.
Bet. Watson would call this reckless.
raise: Raise. I find I am not bored after all.
Raise. Let us raise the stakes, and the interest.
all_in: All in. When you have eliminated the impossible...
Everything. I have faked my own death for less.
All in. A three-pipe problem, settled in one.
reraised: Opposition! Excellent. My mind rebels at stagnation.
You interest me. Very few people do.
win: You see, but you do not observe.
Elementary. I shall not insult you by explaining.
Watson will write this up with far too much romance.
A pretty little problem. I am obliged to you for it.
lose: There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.
That calls for the violin, I think. Late, and loudly.
I was not wrong. I was merely early.
You have taught me something. I shall not forgive you.
win_four_of_a_kind: The sign of four. Watson will want it for a title.
beat_javert: Scotland Yard sends for me, Inspector. Now you see why.
beat_nemo: You were read after all, Captain. Not aloud.
beat_cheshire_cat: The grin stays, I see. The chips do not.
beat_dracula: Vampires in Transylvania. I shall amend the entry.
beat_caesar: You should have read the note, Caesar.
beat_the_ai: Record it, machine. I shall remember it better.
